newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU's Rauen-German tax revenues to fall further.
newsitem.headline: CDU's Rauen-German tax revenues to fall further.

text.p: A prominent member of Germany's ruling coalition said on Saturday that lower-than-forecast tax revenues will make it even harder for Germany to meet the necessary criteria to join European currency union.

Peter Rauen, a senior member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats and vice-chairman of the government finance committee, said when the German tax estimates are released in the autumn, they will show tax revenues lower by double-digit billions of marks.

Rauen said in an advance copy of an interview from the Sonntag-Express newspaper that 3.5 billion marks more would have to go to the Federal Labour Office because of high unemployment, while income from social insurance contributions fell at the same time.
He said that lower tax revenues would cause problems for Germany meeting the Maastricht treaty criteria for European currency union membership, given Germany's already tight budgetary situation.

In an interview with the news magazine Spiegel, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said that tax revenues were in line with forecasts made in May. These estimates forecast a fall in tax revenues of 18 billion marks.
